messages.subject: Problem with Histogram
parts:
Dear All,
I am trying to plot a histogram using a log scale.
This is reminiscent of another post of mine, see e.g.

http://bit.ly/diXGBA

when Hadley told me that it does not make sense to use log coordinates
on the y axis of a histogram.
Leaving aside the meaningfulness of what I am doing, in the past (i.e.
with version 0.8.7) I was able, running the same script at the end of
the email, to get vertical bars all starting from 10^0=1. Now, instead,
I get also some inverted bars. Is this a bug or a new feature of 0.8.8
(automatic detection of empty bins?).
I would like to know just to find out whether I have to resort to
geom_hist for this kind of plots in the future.
Many thanks

Lorenzo


##################################################################################################################

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1234)

my_dframe <- rlnorm(10000,1,1.2)

my_dframe <- as.data.frame(my_dframe)

names(my_dframe) <- c("time")

my_max <- max(my_dframe)*10.
my_min <- min(my_dframe)


gpl <- ggplot(my_dframe,aes(x=time) )+
opts( panel.background=theme_rect(fill='white', size=1.5))+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
geom_histogram(aes(y=..count..), binwidth=.2, colour="black",
fill="blue")+
opts( panel.background=theme_rect(fill='white', size=1.5))+
opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black",
size=1),axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"))+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
## geom_vline(xintercept = log10(60), col="red", size=1)+
## geom_vline(xintercept = log10(600), col="darkgreen",size=1)+
ylab("y var")+
xlab("x")+
scale_x_continuous(trans="log10",limits=c(my_min,my_max))+
scale_y_continuous(trans="log10") +
opts(axis.title.x = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 35, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=30, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=30, colour="black", hjust=1))

pdf("test_hist.pdf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()
